paragraphs: CLIP’s ability to classify images under distribution shifts does not fully describe its reliability. This paper examines three separate questions: whether predictions withstand changes in visual factors, whether confidence estimates match actual correctness, and whether models recognize anomalous inputs. These questions broaden evaluation beyond classification accuracy to properties relevant when interpreting and trusting predictions.

The study compares 83 CLIP models with 127 ImageNet classifiers, covering different architectures, training data, and training strategies. Its evaluation includes 10 visual factors, five kinds of out-of-distribution data, and eight challenging test conditions. This breadth lets the authors examine reliability across several kinds of change instead of treating robustness as a single characteristic.

One finding is that CLIP models do not consistently provide better-calibrated confidence estimates than other ImageNet models, contrary to earlier findings. The study also identifies training source design as influential across all three properties. Its practical message is that strong generalization alone does not establish reliable confidence or anomaly detection; these properties need their own evaluation.
neurips-2023-a-closer-look-at-the-robust.tldr: A broad comparison finds that CLIP’s strong generalization does not consistently translate into better-calibrated uncertainty, and training sources strongly influence reliability.

paragraphs: Vertical federated learning lets participants jointly train a model while retaining their private data. Zeroth-order optimization offers a way to conceal internal model information without expensive additional privacy mechanisms, but its slower convergence can require more communication. This paper addresses both that efficiency problem and the lack of a theoretical explanation for its privacy protection.

The proposed approach combines two optimization methods within the training process. It applies a zeroth-order gradient at clients’ output layers, identified as especially important for privacy, while using first-order gradients elsewhere. This selective arrangement preserves the privacy protection attributed to zeroth-order optimization while improving convergence, rather than applying the slower approach throughout the model.

The authors also prove an equivalence between applying zeroth-order optimization in their VFL analysis and adding a Gaussian mechanism to gradient information, providing an implicit differential privacy guarantee. Experiments report utility similar to the Gaussian mechanism at the same privacy budget, alongside substantially lower communication costs than the compared communication-efficient VFL frameworks. The contribution therefore connects an optimization design with both privacy analysis and practical communication savings.
neurips-2023-a-unified-solution-for-priv.tldr: Hybrid optimization concentrates zeroth-order updates at client outputs to improve federated training efficiency while supporting an implicit differential privacy guarantee.

paragraphs: A synthetic medical image can look realistic while depicting clinically implausible features. The paper argues that general image-quality scores cannot adequately assess this distinction because they do not incorporate clinical knowledge. Anticipating every possible clinical error is also difficult, making a fixed collection of automated checks an incomplete answer to the assessment problem.

The authors introduce a three-stage process centered on pathologist feedback. First, a conditional diffusion model learns to generate images associated with a clinical concept. Pathologists then evaluate whether generated images meet clinical requirements. A reward model learns to predict these judgments on new images, and its predictions become part of the objective used to fine-tune the generator.

The reported results show significant improvements in fidelity, diversity, usefulness for downstream applications, and expert-assessed plausibility. Feedback also teaches the generator clinical concepts that were not annotated in its original training data. This demonstrates how expert judgments can supply information beyond existing labels and guide image generation toward clinically meaningful qualities that visual realism alone does not capture.
neurips-2023-aligning-synthetic-medical-.tldr: Pathologist feedback guides diffusion-model fine-tuning, improving synthetic medical images and teaching clinical concepts absent from the original annotations.

paragraphs: Generative adversarial networks can be expensive to train and run, motivating methods that reduce computation while retaining useful performance. Dynamic sparse training is one candidate, with encouraging results in supervised learning. Applying it to GANs introduces an additional challenge: training involves a generator and a discriminator whose adversarial interaction must remain productive as the networks become sparse.

The paper introduces a metric called the balance ratio to examine the relationship between the sparse generator and discriminator. This gives the authors a way to study their training balance explicitly. The proposed method, ADAPT, then seeks to control that ratio during dynamic sparse training, making the interaction between the two networks part of the efficiency strategy.

Experiments on multiple datasets produce promising results for the method. The stated aim is a useful trade-off between generation performance and computational cost, rather than a claim that sparsity removes all training difficulties. The contribution is to treat adversarial balance as a central consideration when adapting sparse training to GANs.
neurips-2023-balanced-training-for-spars.tldr: ADAPT uses a balance metric to coordinate sparse GAN training and pursue a better trade-off between performance and computational cost.

paragraphs: Fair clustering can impose demographic requirements on different parts of a solution. Group fairness asks each cluster to approximately reflect the population’s demographic composition. Diversity in center selection instead asks the selected centers to reflect that composition. This paper studies how these two requirements interact, addressing a gap left when fairness criteria are considered separately.

The authors show that a constant-factor approximation algorithm for either requirement can be used to obtain a constant-factor approximation satisfying both. They also establish an important asymmetry: any solution already satisfying group fairness can be modified to satisfy center diversity with a bounded increase in clustering cost. Starting from a center-diverse solution does not support the same general post-processing guarantee.

The paper further shows that these demographic requirements can conflict with a collection of distance-based fairness notions. In worst-case instances, no solution satisfies the relevant requirements together. Experiments support the theoretical findings. The results clarify both a constructive route for combining demographic constraints and a reason that adding other fairness requirements can make a clustering problem infeasible.
neurips-2023-doubly-constrained-fair-clu.tldr: Two demographic clustering constraints can be combined with constant-factor guarantees, but their relationship is asymmetric and other fairness requirements can create infeasibility.

paragraphs: FaceComposer brings several kinds of facial content creation into one generative model: producing faces from text, editing faces through written instructions, and animating them. Its central aim is to make these capabilities work together, allowing a shared model to support both individual tasks and some combinations of them.

The approach builds on latent diffusion and compositional generation, combining different conditions to guide the output. These include identity features and a face-specific representation called Projected Normalized Coordinate Code. This gives the model several kinds of facial information to work with alongside text, supporting the broader goal of flexible control over generated content.

To support text instructions and animation, the researchers cleaned existing face-image datasets and collected roughly 500 hours of talking-face video. They added temporal self-attention to the U-Net, enabling the model to learn denoising from a mixture of still images and videos.

The reported experiments suggest performance comparable to or better than leading methods on individual tasks. Some combined tasks can also run in a single forward pass, supporting the model’s potential as a general foundation for face generation. A user interface brings creation, editing, and animation into one service.
neurips-2023-facecomposer-a-unified-mode.tldr: FaceComposer combines text-controlled face creation, editing, and animation in one diffusion model, with experiments suggesting competitive performance across individual tasks.

paragraphs: MCMC methods generate samples intended to approximate a target probability distribution, but their theoretical convergence can be slow for non-log-concave targets. This creates a tension with their practical usefulness. The paper studies a more focused question: whether the distribution of sampled states, conditioned on being inside a particular region, can become accurate quickly.

The central result assumes that a Poincaré-style inequality holds within the chosen subset of the state space. Under this condition, the conditional distribution of MCMC iterates converges rapidly to the target’s conditional distribution on that subset. The authors formalize this statement and quantify its rate, including situations where convergence across the entire state space is provably slow.

The distinction matters because local conditional accuracy and global accuracy are different objectives. The result does not require rapid global mixing to establish the former. The paper explores implications for sampling Gaussian mixtures, estimating parameters of Gaussian mixture models, and Gibbs sampling with well-connected local minima, showing how this conditional perspective can inform several sampling and estimation problems.
neurips-2023-fast-conditional-mixing-of-.tldr: Under a regional Poincaré-style condition, MCMC can rapidly approximate a conditional distribution even when global convergence is provably slow.

paragraphs: An reinforcement learning agent can use external policies as sources of knowledge about a task. Existing approaches can improve learning efficiency this way, but combining or replacing those policies remains difficult. This paper introduces Knowledge-Grounded RL to make the use of multiple knowledge policies both efficient and flexible, motivated by how people learn from observing others.

Its main architectural contribution is the Knowledge-Inclusive Attention Network, or KIAN. The network uses embeddings and attention to predict actions while allowing the available knowledge policies to be rearranged. This makes flexibility in the set of knowledge sources part of the actor’s design, rather than assuming a fixed combination throughout its use.

KIAN also introduces a policy-distribution design addressing entropy imbalance, which the authors identify as an obstacle to exploration in maximum-entropy Knowledge-Grounded RL. Experiments show that KIAN outperforms alternative methods using external knowledge policies and supports efficient, flexible learning. Human-like efficiency is the motivation for the paradigm; the stated findings concern the tested reinforcement learning methods and their ability to incorporate outside policies.
neurips-2023-flexible-attention-based-mu.tldr: KIAN uses attention to combine rearrangeable knowledge policies and addresses an exploration imbalance to improve reinforcement learning efficiency.

paragraphs: Nonlinear independent component analysis seeks hidden sources from observations formed by mixing those sources nonlinearly. The central theoretical question is identifiability: whether the observations can determine the underlying sources. Without additional assumptions, this is impossible. Earlier work uses sparse connections between sources and observations, but practical settings may violate sparsity, source independence, or assumptions about the mixing process.

This paper develops identifiability results for broader settings. These include having more observed variables than sources, called undercompleteness, and allowing some sources to depart from sparsity or independence assumptions. It also examines flexible grouping structures, including cases where some sources form independent groups of different sizes that cannot be divided into smaller independent groups.

The contribution is a set of guarantees adapted to these structures, rather than an assumption-free solution to nonlinear source recovery. The authors support their theoretical claims with synthetic and real-world experiments. The findings expand the circumstances in which meaningful recovery guarantees can be established when the full collection of classical ICA assumptions does not hold.
neurips-2023-generalizing-nonlinear-ica-.tldr: New identifiability results extend nonlinear source recovery to undercomplete settings, partial sparsity, some source dependence, and flexible independent groups.

paragraphs: Adapter methods tune a vision-language model for a new task by adding relatively few parameters, which is useful when task-specific data are scarce. The paper identifies two shortcomings in many existing adapters: using only one modality to model task knowledge and overlooking relationships among the task’s classes. GraphAdapter addresses both through an explicit graph representation.

The method builds two connected sources of structural knowledge: a textual knowledge subgraph and a visual knowledge subgraph. In each, nodes represent classes or semantics, while edges represent correlations between them. A textual adapter uses this dual structure so that each prompt’s text features can incorporate class relationships from both language and images.

The resulting features form a more effective classifier for downstream tasks in the authors’ experiments. Across 11 benchmark datasets, GraphAdapter significantly outperforms the compared adapter-based approaches. The finding supports incorporating relationships between classes into efficient adaptation, with visual information contributing directly to the refinement of textual features rather than leaving the adapter’s task knowledge confined to one modality.
neurips-2023-graphadapter-tuning-vision-.tldr: GraphAdapter improves efficient vision-language adaptation by using both visual and textual class relationships to refine prompt features.

paragraphs: Active learning lets a model choose which unlabeled examples should receive labels while staying within a labeling budget. Choosing those examples requires a query strategy, and different strategies work better under different conditions and budgets. This paper addresses the practical problem of selecting a strategy for the situation at hand rather than assuming one choice will remain suitable.

The proposed solution is a derivative-based method for dynamically selecting an active learning strategy. It takes both the characteristics of the problem and the available budget into account. A theoretical analysis of a simplified scenario provides intuition for the approach, connecting the selection method to an understandable setting before applying it to more varied tasks.

Experiments across computer vision tasks and different budgets demonstrate the approach’s effectiveness. The findings support adapting strategy selection to the learning situation instead of treating it as a fixed preliminary decision. The theoretical motivation comes from the simplified analysis, while the broader evidence is empirical; the abstract does not establish a universal guarantee of choosing the best strategy in every setting.
neurips-2023-how-to-select-which-active-.tldr: A derivative-based method dynamically selects active learning strategies according to the problem and labeling budget, with support from computer vision experiments.

paragraphs: This paper applies AI to universal algebra conjectures that have both equational and topological descriptions. The topological view makes graph-based analysis possible, but ordinary graph neural networks can be difficult to interpret. For mathematical investigation, accurate predictions alone are insufficient: researchers also need explanations that can help assess existing conjectures or suggest new ones.

The authors develop an algorithm that generates datasets from these conjectures and introduce a neural layer for constructing fully interpretable graph networks. The two contributions connect mathematical problem formulation with a model designed to expose understandable structure. This makes interpretation part of the learning approach rather than relying solely on explanations added after a prediction.

Experiments report improved interpretability without sacrificing task accuracy, along with strong generalization when predicting universal algebra properties. The networks produce simple explanations that provide empirical support for existing conjectures and identify subgraphs suggesting new conjectures. These results describe a tool for mathematical exploration: empirical validation and candidate conjectures remain distinct from a mathematical proof that a statement always holds.
neurips-2023-interpretable-graph-network.tldr: Interpretable graph networks provide empirical support for universal algebra conjectures and identify structures that suggest new ones.

paragraphs: A network is equivariant when transforming its input produces a corresponding transformation of its output. A common way to achieve this is to make individual layers equivariant. This paper asks whether the reverse implication holds: if an entire ReLU network respects a symmetry, must that symmetry also be respected separately by all its layers?

The theoretical answer is conditional. The authors identify cases where whole-network equivariance does imply layerwise equivariance, but also demonstrate that this is false in general. They nevertheless conjecture that convolutional networks trained to be equivariant will exhibit equivariance layer by layer. They relate this conjecture to a weaker version of an existing permutation conjecture about neural networks.

Quantitative experiments with VGG networks on CIFAR10 and qualitative experiments with ResNets on ImageNet illustrate and support the theoretical analysis. The authors also find that merging a network with a group-transformed version of itself is typically easier than merging two different networks. This provides another perspective on symmetry and network merging while leaving the proposed training-related statement as a conjecture.
neurips-2023-investigating-how-relu-netw.tldr: Whole-network equivariance does not generally imply equivariant layers, though theory and experiments motivate a conjecture about trained convolutional networks.

paragraphs: Deep ensembles combine several neural networks to improve prediction. Although the final goal is good performance from the combined ensemble, individual networks are commonly trained independently. This paper investigates why directly optimizing the ensemble’s shared loss can behave poorly, despite appearing to target the desired outcome more directly.

The authors separate the ensemble objective into two components: the strength of individual learners and the diversity among them. Their analysis reveals a failure mode called learner collusion. During joint optimization, networks can coordinate in ways that inflate apparent diversity on training data without producing differences that remain useful on unseen data. This pseudo-diversity leads to a larger generalization gap.

The paper demonstrates practical consequences across standard machine learning tasks and architectures by gradually varying training between independent optimization and joint optimization. This experimental design connects the failure to the degree of joint training. The contribution explains how an apparently favorable ensemble objective can reward misleading training-set behavior, helping account for the established practice of training ensemble members separately.
neurips-2023-joint-training-of-deep-ense.tldr: Joint ensemble training can encourage learners to manufacture diversity that fits training data but fails to generalize.

paragraphs: Learning and memory are associated with local changes at synapses, but discovering rules for those changes becomes difficult when several rules operate together. This paper develops filter SBI, a simulation-based inference method for exploring families of co-active plasticity rules in recurrent spiking networks. Candidate rules pass through progressively finer constraints that can be changed during the search.

The authors first investigate flexible doublet, or Hebbian, rules. The inferred family contains solutions that extend and refine predictions from mean-field theory, as well as solutions that reject some predictions. They then represent rules with multilayer perceptrons that combine factors such as synaptic weight, voltage, triplets, and co-dependency, allowing a richer search space.

Among millions of possible rules, the method identifies thousands of distinct combinations satisfying biological constraints, including plausible activity and weight dynamics. These are candidate mechanisms for further investigation, rather than a uniquely established account of biological learning. The results also suggest refinements and predictions for classical plasticity experiments, connecting computational exploration with questions that could guide subsequent studies.
neurips-2023-meta-learning-families-of-p.tldr: Filter SBI searches families of interacting synaptic plasticity rules and finds thousands of combinations consistent with specified biological constraints.

paragraphs: Selecting a pretrained model for a new task can be expensive when a model collection contains many different architectures and capabilities. Evaluating every candidate through forward or backward passes adds substantial work. Model Spider addresses this selection problem by learning representations that make it possible to estimate how well a model and task fit together.

The method summarizes both pretrained models and tasks as vectors. Using approximate model performance on a separate collection of training tasks, it learns these representations and a score for each model-task pair. The learned ranking ability transfers to new tasks. It then uses the highest-ranked candidates to enrich the task representation with model-specific information and reranks the candidates.

This staged process balances efficient initial selection with a more informed refinement step. The authors report promising performance across diverse model collections, including visual models and large language models. The contribution is a learned approach to model selection that uses experience from earlier tasks and targeted candidate information to reduce the burden of assessing a large model zoo.
neurips-2023-model-spider-learning-to-ra.tldr: Model Spider learns vector representations of models and tasks to rank pretrained candidates efficiently, then refines rankings using leading candidates.

paragraphs: A policy recommendation does not guarantee that someone takes the recommended treatment. People can differ both in their willingness to participate and in how much they benefit. This paper studies how to evaluate and learn encouragement policies when those differences matter and when decision-makers also care about the distribution of access and outcomes.

The framework covers identification, doubly robust estimation, and estimation robust to possible positivity violations, where relevant treatment or recommendation possibilities may have insufficient support. It uses constrained optimization to incorporate requirements such as demographic parity in treatment uptake. An extension to algorithmic recommendations relies on a covariate-conditional exclusion restriction and includes robustness checks for insufficient recommendation support.

The authors develop a two-stage algorithm based on online learning for overparameterized policy classes under general constraints, obtaining regret bounds that account for variance. A stylized case study examines recommendations for supervised release in a pretrial risk-assessment tool while reducing surveillance disparities. The central contribution is to optimize recommendations with human uptake and fairness constraints explicitly included, rather than equating a recommendation with the action ultimately taken.
neurips-2023-optimal-and-fair-encouragem.tldr: The paper develops methods for evaluating and learning fair recommendation policies that account for varying treatment uptake and benefits.

paragraphs: This paper connects two ways of learning neural networks: minimizing training error with gradient descent and Bayesian learning through importance sampling. Its central concern is the relationship between generalization and computational efficiency. In the comparison developed by the authors, Bayesian learning generalizes better but samples inefficiently, while optimization offers better sampling efficiency with poorer generalization.

The theoretical analysis derives an algorithm-dependent PAC-Bayesian generalization bound for infinitely wide networks. It uses an exact KL divergence between a Gaussian prior and the trained posterior produced by gradient descent with an infinitesimal step size. Those conditions define the setting of the result and are important when interpreting what the bound establishes.

The authors also show that adding a weight can transform gradient-based optimization into importance sampling. This connection motivates Transformative Bayesian Learning, called TansBL, which allows a trade-off between the two approaches. The contribution is both an analytical bridge and an algorithmic way to balance generalization against sampling efficiency within the framework studied.
neurips-2023-optimization-and-bayes-a-tr.tldr: TansBL connects gradient optimization with Bayesian importance sampling to trade sampling efficiency against generalization.

paragraphs: The paper studies reinforcement learning in continuous time and space, with random system dynamics described by a stochastic differential equation. The objective extends over an infinite horizon while discounting future rewards. This setting requires mathematical tools suited to continuous evolution when analyzing how changing a policy changes its expected performance.

The authors develop a notion of occupation time tailored to the discounted objective. It describes time spent across the system’s states while accounting for the discounting of later behavior. They use this construction to derive performance-difference formulas and local approximations, creating a basis for comparing policies and reasoning about nearby policy changes.

These results are then extended to policy gradient, trust region policy optimization, and proximal policy optimization. Those methods are established in discrete reinforcement learning but less developed in the continuous setting considered here. Numerical experiments demonstrate effectiveness and advantages of the proposed approach. The contribution links continuous-time analysis to practical policy-optimization methods under the specified stochastic dynamics and discounted objective.
neurips-2023-policy-optimization-for-con.tldr: A discounted occupation-time formulation supports policy comparison and policy-optimization methods for reinforcement learning in continuous time and space.

paragraphs: Generating three-dimensional humans with diffusion models is challenging because 3D representations can be computationally expensive and human bodies have articulated structure. PrimDiffusion addresses these issues through its representation: it models the body as a collection of small volumes carrying radiance and kinematic information, then performs diffusion directly over those volumetric primitives.

This design provides a compact but expressive parameter space and incorporates prior structure about humans. It also supports rendering without a decoder, enabling synthesis from new viewpoints and in new poses. The approach combines the representational capacity of volumes with the rendering efficiency associated with primitives, making representation design central to both generation and subsequent use.

Experiments report better 3D human generation than the compared state-of-the-art methods. After denoising is complete, the generated humans can be rendered in real time at 512 by 512 resolution; the real-time claim applies to rendering after generation. The authors also demonstrate conditional generation without additional training, including texture transfer and 3D inpainting, illustrating the flexibility of the representation.
neurips-2023-primdiffusion-volumetric-pr.tldr: PrimDiffusion generates 3D humans through volumetric primitives, enabling flexible manipulation and real-time rendering after denoising.

paragraphs: In standard multiple instance learning, an example is a bag of items. A bag is positive exactly when it contains at least one positive item. This rule creates an asymmetry: evidence for a positive item determines the bag’s label, and swapping the meaning of positive and negative changes the task. The paper examines whether prominent deep-learning models respect that assumption.

The authors evaluate five deep multiple instance learning models and find that none consistently adheres to the standard rule. The models can learn the opposite pattern, treating bags as positive until a negative counterexample appears. Such behavior can fit correlations while violating the intended relationship between individual items and the bag label.

To reveal this problem, the authors propose algorithmic unit tests using synthetic datasets solvable by models that respect the assumption. Each evaluated method fails at least one test. The tests offer a model-agnostic way to check semantic behavior beyond predictive performance. The authors suspect related models may share the issue, while their demonstrated findings concern the five examined methods.
neurips-2023-reproducibility-in-multiple.tldr: Synthetic algorithmic unit tests show that five prominent deep multiple instance learning models can violate the task’s defining label assumption.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can produce high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs, but many require hundreds or thousands of sampling steps. Accelerating an existing sampling process can reduce output quality and introduce blur. ResShift addresses the source of this cost by designing a diffusion process for super-resolution that needs fewer steps from the outset.

The method constructs a Markov chain connecting high-resolution and low-resolution images by progressively shifting the residual, or difference, between them. This makes the transition directly reflect the super-resolution task. A specially designed noise schedule controls both how quickly the residual shifts and how much noise enters the process, providing flexibility in the transition.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show performance superior to or at least comparable with the state-of-the-art methods considered, using only 20 sampling steps. The result supports redesigning the diffusion process around the relationship between input and output images. Its efficiency comes from the proposed transition itself, avoiding the need to rely on a separate inference-time acceleration procedure.
neurips-2023-resshift-efficient-diffusio.tldr: ResShift redesigns diffusion around the difference between low- and high-resolution images, achieving competitive super-resolution with 20 sampling steps.

paragraphs: The paper asks how many information queries are needed to learn equilibria in zero-sum games with K actions per player. In the studied query model, a player observes the expected payoff of every action against the opponent’s randomized choice. The challenge is to characterize the required number of queries as both game size and desired accuracy change.

For exact equilibria, the authors establish that query complexity grows linearly with K. This is essentially as costly as querying the entire payoff matrix. Approximate equilibria are more subtle: the existing upper bound is the smaller of order log(K) divided by the error tolerance and order K, but matching lower bounds remain unresolved.

The authors show why a broad lower-bound strategy fails: matrices with entries from a known countable set can be fully identified using one query in this model. They introduce a different technique yielding a logarithmic-type lower bound for sufficiently small errors, specifically errors at most 1/(cK⁴). This advances the approximate case without closing its gap between upper and lower bounds.
neurips-2023-towards-characterizing-the-.tldr: Exact zero-sum equilibria require linearly many queries, while a new lower-bound technique advances the still-unresolved approximate case.

paragraphs: Evaluating whether language models reason about human mental states is difficult when earlier tests produce inconsistent results or have questionable validity. This paper introduces a way to generate social-reasoning evaluations by having language models populate causal templates. The approach gives the evaluation process a structured basis while allowing many individual examples to be produced.

The resulting benchmark, BigToM, contains 5,000 model-written evaluations and 25 controls. Human participants rate its quality above earlier crowd-sourced evaluations and comparable to expert-written evaluations. This quality assessment addresses the construction of the benchmark separately from the question of how well language models perform on it.

The authors then compare several language models with human performance. Their results suggest that GPT4 exhibits theory-of-mind inference patterns resembling those of humans, but does so less reliably, while other models struggle. The conclusion concerns observed social reasoning on these evaluations. It preserves a distinction between similarity in inference patterns and consistently matching human performance, which the reported results do not establish.
neurips-2023-understanding-social-reason.tldr: BigToM uses causal templates to evaluate social reasoning and finds evidence of human-like but less reliable inference patterns in GPT4.

paragraphs: Real-world graphs combine connections with rich attributes on different kinds of nodes and links. Modeling all of this uniformly is difficult, and graph neural networks often need substantial training for particular prediction tasks. WalkLM seeks generic, unsupervised node representations that jointly capture graph structure and attribute meaning without being tied to one downstream task.

The framework first performs random walks that retain attribute information. An automated procedure converts those walks into roughly meaningful text sequences. A language model is then fine-tuned on the sequences, and its embedding vectors become the graph representations. The text therefore carries both information about the entities and information about how the walks connect them.

Experiments evaluate the learned node embeddings on multiple prediction tasks across real-world attributed graphs. The authors observe significant improvements over a broad set of state-of-the-art unsupervised node embedding methods. The results support using language-model training as a common mechanism for combining semantic attributes with graph structure, while preserving the ability to reuse the resulting representations for different tasks.
neurips-2023-walklm-a-uniform-language-m.tldr: WalkLM turns attributed graph walks into text and fine-tunes a language model to produce reusable node embeddings capturing semantics and structure.
